title.en: Who says what in a meeting
title.es: Quién dice qué en una reunión

es: Identificar quién dirige, quién anota y qué función cumple cada intervención en una reunión de vecinos.

teaching.en: Whoever agrees to chair the meeting should open the session, read out each item on the agenda in order and give every member a fair turn to speak.
teaching.es: Quien acepta presidir la reunión debe abrir la sesión, leer cada punto del orden del día por orden y dar a cada miembro un turno justo para hablar.
teaching.explanationEs: Chair the meeting: abrir, dar turnos y cerrar. Item es cada punto del orden del día (agenda).
segments: Whoever agrees to chair the meeting should open the session, read out each item
on the agenda in order and give every member a fair turn to speak.
teaching.audioText: Whoever agrees to chair the meeting should open the session, read out each item on the agenda in order and give every member a fair turn to speak.

teaching.en: The secretary writes the minutes while the discussion is still going on, so that anyone who missed the session can see what was decided and by whom.
teaching.es: La secretaria redacta el acta mientras la discusión sigue en marcha, para que quien faltó a la sesión pueda ver qué se decidió y quién lo decidió.
teaching.explanationEs: Minutes es el acta escrita, nunca «minutos» en este contexto.
segments: The secretary writes the minutes while the discussion is still going on, so that
anyone who missed the session can see what was decided and by whom.
teaching.audioText: The secretary writes the minutes while the discussion is still going on, so that anyone who missed the session can see what was decided and by whom.

teaching.en: If a speaker begins to digress, the chair may politely steer the discussion back by saying that the new point belongs under a different item.
teaching.es: Si alguien empieza a divagar, quien preside puede reconducir la discusión con educación diciendo que el nuevo punto pertenece a otro apartado.
teaching.explanationEs: Digress: salirse del tema. Steer back: devolver la conversación a su cauce.
segments: If a speaker begins to digress, the chair may politely steer the discussion
back by saying that the new point belongs under a different item.
teaching.audioText: If a speaker begins to digress, the chair may politely steer the discussion back by saying that the new point belongs under a different item.

teaching.en: Members who wish to take the floor should wait to be recognised, because it is considered rude to interrupt a colleague who is still speaking.
teaching.es: Los miembros que quieran tomar la palabra deben esperar a que se les conceda, porque se considera de mala educación interrumpir a un compañero que aún habla.
teaching.explanationEs: Take the floor: empezar a hablar con el permiso de la presidencia.
segments: Members who wish to take the floor should wait to be recognised, because
it is considered rude to interrupt a colleague who is still speaking.
teaching.audioText: Members who wish to take the floor should wait to be recognised, because it is considered rude to interrupt a colleague who is still speaking.

teaching.en: Sorry to interrupt, but could I clarify one point before the chair decides to call for a vote on the proposal?
teaching.es: Perdona que interrumpa, pero ¿podría aclarar un punto antes de que la presidencia decida pedir que se vote la propuesta?
teaching.explanationEs: Sorry to + verbo base pide permiso; could I clarify suaviza la petición; call for a vote somete algo a votación.
segments: Sorry to interrupt, but could I clarify one point before the
chair decides to call for a vote on the proposal?
teaching.audioText: Sorry to interrupt, but could I clarify one point before the chair decides to call for a vote on the proposal?

teaching.en: Once the debate is over, any member may propose a motion, and the chair will call for a vote only after somebody has seconded it.
teaching.es: Cuando termina el debate, cualquier miembro puede proponer una moción, y la presidencia pedirá la votación solo después de que alguien la secunde.
teaching.explanationEs: Propose a motion abre una propuesta formal; la votación llega cuando alguien la apoya (second).
segments: Once the debate is over, any member may propose a motion, and the
chair will call for a vote only after somebody has seconded it.
teaching.audioText: Once the debate is over, any member may propose a motion, and the chair will call for a vote only after somebody has seconded it.

prompt.es: Lee la intervención de Ana en el acta. ¿Qué función cumple?

choices.text: She opens the session and explains how the evening will run.
She proposes a motion and asks the members to decide on it.
She interrupts a speaker to correct something said earlier.

feedback.es: Ana saluda, presenta el orden del día y asigna el acta: abre la sesión, tarea propia de quien preside. No propone ni interrumpe.

hint.es: Piensa en qué hace quien preside al comenzar, antes de que nadie haya hablado.

origin.text: Ana: Good evening, everyone. Before we begin, let me remind you that we have three items on the agenda tonight and that Sara will write the minutes. Let's start with the new bench.

prompt.es: Completa: «Leo, creo que te estás saliendo del tema de este punto.»

feedback.es: Digress from es la colocación para apartarse del tema principal: lo que hace Leo al contar sus vacaciones.

hint.es: Es el verbo que significa salirse del tema; tras to va la forma base.

origin.text: Leo has been describing his summer holiday for ten minutes now. Ana smiles and says, «Leo, I think you are starting to ___ from the item we are discussing.»

prompt.es: Ordena: «Cada miembro debe esperar a la presidencia antes de tomar la palabra.»

answer.text: Each member must wait for the chair before they take the floor

feedback.es: Take the floor es la colocación de empezar a hablar con permiso; must wait for the chair marca la obligación de esperar.

hint.es: Empieza por el sujeto Each member y acaba con la colocación del turno de palabra.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hizo la presidencia cuando un miembro se fue por las ramas.

choices.text: She suggested a separate motion about the parking fines.
She brought the discussion back to the item in hand.
She asked the secretary to read the minutes aloud again.

feedback.es: La presidencia reconduce el debate al punto que tocaba («steered the discussion back»). Las multas de aparcamiento quedan fuera del tema.

origin.audio: At last night's residents' meeting, the chair opened the session by thanking everyone for coming and reading out the three items on the agenda. The secretary, who was writing the minutes, reminded the members that anyone wishing to take the floor should raise a hand first. Halfway through the first item, one member went off the subject and began talking about parking fines, so the chair politely steered the discussion back. A second member then proposed a motion about the bench, and, once it had been seconded, the chair asked everyone to vote.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué ocurrió justo antes de la votación.

choices.text: The secretary read out last month's minutes.
The chair announced the end of the meeting.
Somebody backed the motion about the bench.

feedback.es: La moción sobre el banco fue secundada («had been seconded») y solo entonces se votó; el acta y el cierre no se mencionan en ese momento.

prompt.es: Según el acta, ¿qué función cumple la intervención de Tom?

choices.text: He cuts in politely to ask about the cost.
He takes the floor to propose a separate motion on water.
He closes the item and moves on to the next one.

feedback.es: «Sorry to interrupt… could I clarify…?» es la fórmula de quien corta con cortesía para aclarar un dato; aquí, quién paga el agua.

origin.text: Item 2: the community garden. Mia: I would like to propose that we open the garden on Saturdays. Tom: Sorry to interrupt, Mia, but could I clarify one point? Who pays for the water? Mia: The council does. Leo: That is a fair point, but we are drifting; the water is a separate item. Ana: Thank you, Leo. Let us return to Mia's proposal and ask the members to decide.

prompt.es: En ese acta, ¿qué da a entender Leo con su comentario sobre el agua?

choices.text: That the council should not pay for the garden water.
That the water question belongs under another item.
That Mia should drop her proposal about Saturdays.

feedback.es: Leo admite que la pregunta es razonable, pero dice que es «a separate item»: pertenece a otro punto. Ana lo confirma al volver a la propuesta de Mia.

origin.text: Item 2: the community garden. Mia: I would like to propose that we open the garden on Saturdays. Tom: Sorry to interrupt, Mia, but could I clarify one point? Who pays for the water? Mia: The council does. Leo: That is a fair point, but we are drifting; the water is a separate item. Ana: Thank you, Leo. Let us return to Mia's proposal and ask the members to decide.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué pretende la presidencia con este mensaje.

choices.text: To blame Tom for waiting so long before speaking.
To postpone the decision on the motion until next month.
To limit Mia's turn politely so the meeting keeps moving.

feedback.es: La presidencia pide a Mia que concluya y da paso a Tom sin reprocharle nada: gestiona el tiempo con cortesía. La moción no se aplaza.

origin.audio: Right, that is the first item finished. Before we move on, may I remind everyone that we are already ten minutes over time? Mia, you have held the floor for quite a while, and Tom has been waiting patiently to speak. So, Mia, if you could wrap up in one sentence, Tom can ask his question, and after that we will put the motion to the members.

prompt.es: Completa: «Si nadie quiere añadir nada, pediré que se vote la propuesta.»

feedback.es: Call for a vote es la colocación fija para pedir que se someta algo a votación; con ask se diría ask for a vote.

origin.text: After a long and careful debate, the members agreed that the proposal was clear. The chair looked around the room and said, «If nobody wishes to add anything, I will ___ for a vote on the proposal.»

prompt.es: Según el acta, ¿qué deja claro la presidencia en su respuesta a Carlos?

choices.text: That his objection came too late to change the result.
That the vote must be repeated because of his objection.
That the secretary should remove the vote from the minutes.

feedback.es: Ana recuerda que las objeciones se plantean antes de votar: la decisión ya está tomada y se mantiene. No pide repetir la votación ni borrarla del acta.

origin.text: Minutes, item 4. Sara proposed moving the summer party to June. The members voted, and the proposal was approved. Carlos then objected that the hall would not be free that month. Ana, as chair, replied that objections must be raised before a vote, so the decision would stand.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué hace el hablante con su intervención.

choices.text: He proposes a motion on the parking problem.
He brings the meeting back politely to the planned item.
He asks the secretary to read back the last minutes.

feedback.es: Pide turno con cortesía y propone aparcar el otro tema para volver a lo previsto: reconduce, no propone ni pide el acta.

origin.audio: If I could just come in here for a moment, I think we may be going off the point. The agenda says the bench comes first, and the parking problem is a different matter, so perhaps we could note it down for next month and return to the bench before we run out of time.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Déjame terminar este punto y luego podrás aclarar tu pregunta.»

answer.text: Let me finish this item and then you can clarify your question

feedback.es: Quien preside controla los turnos: let me finish marca que termina primero y then you can clarify cede la palabra después.

title.en: Build on it or push back

es: Sumarse a una propuesta o poner reparos con el lenguaje de consenso y de reserva de una reunión.

teaching.en: I fully support Mia's idea and would gladly endorse it at the next meeting, but first I would like to build on it by suggesting that we test it for a month.
teaching.es: Apoyo por completo la idea de Mia y la respaldaré con gusto en la próxima reunión, pero antes me gustaría desarrollarla sugiriendo que la probemos un mes.
teaching.explanationEs: Build on + idea: partes de lo dicho y añades algo. Support y endorse expresan apoyo; endorse es más formal.
segments: I fully support Mia's idea and would gladly endorse it at the next meeting, but first
I would like to build on it by suggesting that we test it for a month.
teaching.audioText: I fully support Mia's idea and would gladly endorse it at the next meeting, but first I would like to build on it by suggesting that we test it for a month.

teaching.en: That is a fair point, and although it was not my first choice, I can go along with the new date for the sake of the group.
teaching.es: Es un punto razonable y, aunque no era mi primera opción, puedo aceptar la nueva fecha por el bien del grupo.
teaching.explanationEs: Go along with + nombre: aceptas lo propuesto aunque no fuera tu preferencia.
segments: That is a fair point, and although it was not my first choice, I
can go along with the new date for the sake of the group.
teaching.audioText: That is a fair point, and although it was not my first choice, I can go along with the new date for the sake of the group.

teaching.en: I have some reservations about the price, so I am not convinced that the plan is feasible without extra funding from the council.
teaching.es: Tengo algunas reservas sobre el precio, así que no estoy convencido de que el plan sea viable sin más fondos del ayuntamiento.
teaching.explanationEs: Have reservations about + nombre: dudas educadas. Not convinced that + oración: desacuerdo suave.
segments: I have some reservations about the price, so I am not convinced
that the plan is feasible without extra funding from the council.
teaching.audioText: I have some reservations about the price, so I am not convinced that the plan is feasible without extra funding from the council.

teaching.en: In principle I am happy with the proposal, but my main concern is that nobody has said who will pay if the costs rise.
teaching.es: En principio estoy de acuerdo con la propuesta, pero mi principal preocupación es que nadie ha dicho quién pagará si suben los costes.
teaching.explanationEs: In principle concede lo general y prepara la objeción; concern nombra el problema concreto.
segments: In principle I am happy with the proposal, but my main concern
is that nobody has said who will pay if the costs rise.
teaching.audioText: In principle I am happy with the proposal, but my main concern is that nobody has said who will pay if the costs rise.

teaching.en: Rather than vote and leave half the room unhappy, could we reach a compromise that feels fair to both sides, even if nobody gets everything?
teaching.es: En lugar de votar y dejar descontenta a la mitad de la sala, ¿podríamos llegar a un término medio que resulte justo para ambas partes, aunque nadie consiga todo?
teaching.explanationEs: Reach a compromise: llegar a una solución con cesiones mutuas; could we… la propone con suavidad.
segments: Rather than vote and leave half the room unhappy, could we reach a
compromise that feels fair to both sides, even if nobody gets everything?
teaching.audioText: Rather than vote and leave half the room unhappy, could we reach a compromise that feels fair to both sides, even if nobody gets everything?

teaching.en: I have no objection to waiting, provided that the council confirms the budget in writing before anything is signed.
teaching.es: No tengo ninguna objeción a esperar, siempre que el ayuntamiento confirme el presupuesto por escrito antes de firmar nada.
teaching.explanationEs: No objection to + -ing/nombre: aceptación formal; provided that introduce la condición.
segments: I have no objection to waiting, provided that the council
confirms the budget in writing before anything is signed.
teaching.audioText: I have no objection to waiting, provided that the council confirms the budget in writing before anything is signed.

prompt.es: Completa: «Me gustaría desarrollar la idea de Carlos y usar la sala en verano.»

feedback.es: Build on es el verbo con partícula para partir de la idea de otro y añadir algo; Mia no rechaza la propuesta, la amplía.

hint.es: Es el verbo que va con on cuando desarrollas la idea de otra persona.

origin.text: Carlos has suggested using the school hall on Fridays. Mia nods and says, «I would like to ___ on Carlos's idea and use the hall in summer too.»

prompt.es: Tom propone subir la cuota. ¿Qué respuesta expresa una reserva sin cerrar el acuerdo?

choices.text: I see the need, so I have no objection to raising it at all.
I see the need, but I have my doubts about raising it so sharply.
I see the need, but I am simply not willing to discuss it.

feedback.es: Reconoce la necesidad y duda solo del método («reservations about»), sin negarse a hablar. Las otras aceptan del todo o bloquean la conversación.

hint.es: Busca la respuesta que reconoce la necesidad y pone dudas al método, sin rechazar el diálogo.

origin.text: Tom: I suggest we raise the yearly fee to thirty dollars, because the roof needs repairs and the club has no savings.

prompt.es: Ordena: «En principio estoy de acuerdo, pero mi principal preocupación es el coste.»

answer.text: In principle I agree but my main concern is the cost

feedback.es: In principle abre la concesión general y but my main concern introduce la duda concreta.

hint.es: Empieza por la fórmula que concede lo general y termina con lo que te preocupa.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué pedía Leo para los estudiantes.

choices.text: A payment plan paid over several months.
A delay until the roof repairs are finished.
A lower fee for members under eighteen.

feedback.es: Leo pide una cuota menor para menores de dieciocho. El plan de pagos es de Mia y la condición de las reparaciones, de Tom.

origin.audio: At the sports club's monthly meeting, the treasurer proposed raising the yearly fee to cover the cost of a new roof. Leo said he supported the idea in principle, but he was not sure that thirty dollars was realistic for students, and he asked whether the club could find a middle way with a lower fee for members under eighteen. Mia then offered to add to that suggestion with a payment plan, and Tom, who had opposed the fee at first, told the group that he could now go along with it, provided the roof repairs were finished before winter.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige qué condición pone Tom para aceptar la subida.

choices.text: That the repairs are completed before winter begins.
That students always pay less than other members.
That the treasurer shows the accounts once more.

feedback.es: Tom acepta «provided the roof repairs were finished before winter»: la condición es el calendario de las obras, no el precio para estudiantes.

prompt.es: Lee el correo de Sara. ¿Qué actitud muestra hacia el cambio a los jueves?

choices.text: She rejects it, yet tries to sound polite about it.
She accepts it reluctantly but would prefer a compromise.
She welcomes it and has no difficulty with Thursdays.

feedback.es: Sara acepta («no objection», «go along with») pero señala una dificultad y propone alternar días: aceptación a regañadientes que busca un punto medio.

origin.text: Hi all, thanks for circulating the proposal to move our meetings to Thursdays. In principle I have no objection, and I can go along with the change, although Thursdays are hard for me because of my evening class. I wonder whether we could find a middle way and switch between Tuesdays and Thursdays? Either way, I would rather have a decision by the end of the month. Best, Sara

prompt.es: En ese correo, ¿con qué propósito menciona Sara su clase de la tarde?

choices.text: To ask the group to cancel the Thursday meetings completely.
To suggest that other members also attend evening classes.
To explain the difficulty without refusing the change.

feedback.es: Sara da el motivo de su dificultad pero mantiene su aceptación, y por eso propone una solución intermedia en lugar de pedir que se cancele.

origin.text: Hi all, thanks for circulating the proposal to move our meetings to Thursdays. In principle I have no objection, and I can go along with the change, although Thursdays are hard for me because of my evening class. I wonder whether we could find a middle way and switch between Tuesdays and Thursdays? Either way, I would rather have a decision by the end of the month. Best, Sara

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué busca la hablante con su intervención.

choices.text: To hold off on deciding until the real cost is clearer.
To reject the plan on the grounds of its purpose.
To ask the group to approve the budget at once.

feedback.es: Acepta la idea pero duda de las cifras y pide otro presupuesto antes de comprometerse: busca retrasar la decisión hasta conocer el coste real.

origin.audio: I do appreciate the thought that has gone into this, and in principle I am on board. But I have to be honest: I am not convinced the figures are realistic, because the quotes we have seen only cover materials, not the work itself. Could we ask for one more quote before we go any further?

prompt.es: Completa: «No me opongo, pero sí tengo algunas dudas sobre el calendario.»

feedback.es: Have some reservations about es la colocación cortés para dudar sin oponerse; objections sería más fuerte y suele ir con to.

origin.text: Tom did not say no, but he made his doubts clear to the group. «I am not against the plan, but I do have some ___ about the timing.»

prompt.es: Según el diálogo, ¿qué hace Tom con la propuesta de Carlos?

choices.text: He backs the date and adds an idea for raising money.
He doubts that the date is practical and gives a reason.
He objects to the tournament itself and wants it dropped.

feedback.es: Tom duda de la fecha y da un motivo (los jugadores estarán de vacaciones). La idea de recaudar dinero es de Mia, y nadie pide anular el torneo.

origin.text: Carlos: I propose we hold the tournament in July. Mia: I support that, and I think we could use it to raise money for new goals. Tom: I am not convinced that July works, because half the players will be on holiday.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué ha cambiado en la postura de la hablante.

choices.text: She has decided not to vote because the sides cannot agree.
She still rejects both options but will not say so openly.
She has moved from a likely no to backing a middle path.

feedback.es: Venía a votar en contra, pero ve que ambos piden algo razonable y propone un reparto de días: pasa de la oposición a apoyar una solución intermedia.

origin.audio: I will be honest: I came tonight fully planning to vote against this. But after hearing both sides, I can see that neither of you is asking for the impossible. So here is my suggestion: we keep Saturdays as the main day, which is what Leo wants, and Tom gets his Sunday sessions once a month. If nobody has a serious objection, I would be happy to go along with that.

prompt.es: Completa: «Me gusta en principio, pero dudo que sea viable con dos voluntarios.»

feedback.es: Feasible significa viable en la práctica; Sara acepta la idea pero cuestiona si se puede llevar a cabo con tan poca gente.

origin.text: The club wants to open a second café in the park. Sara says, «I like it in principle, but I wonder whether it is really ___ with only two volunteers.»

es: Seguir un debate de vecinos y extraer posturas, propuestas y acciones con responsable y plazo.

teaching.en: Carlos is in favour of the new bike lane, whereas Mia is opposed to it, so the group has not yet reached a consensus on the proposal.
teaching.es: Carlos está a favor del nuevo carril bici, mientras que Mia se opone, así que el grupo aún no ha alcanzado un consenso sobre la propuesta.
teaching.explanationEs: Be in favour of / be opposed to + nombre declara una postura; consensus es el acuerdo de todos sin votar.
segments: Carlos is in favour of the new bike lane, whereas Mia is opposed to
it, so the group has not yet reached a consensus on the proposal.
teaching.audioText: Carlos is in favour of the new bike lane, whereas Mia is opposed to it, so the group has not yet reached a consensus on the proposal.

teaching.en: Leo put forward the proposal, and his position is clear, but I am afraid I cannot agree, because it would cost far more than the council has promised.
teaching.es: Leo presentó la propuesta y su postura está clara, pero me temo que no puedo estar de acuerdo, porque costaría mucho más de lo que el ayuntamiento ha prometido.
teaching.explanationEs: Put forward: presentar una propuesta ante el grupo. I am afraid I cannot agree es un desacuerdo educado; position resume lo que alguien defiende.
segments: Leo put forward the proposal, and his position is clear, but I am afraid
I cannot agree, because it would cost far more than the council has promised.
teaching.audioText: Leo put forward the proposal, and his position is clear, but I am afraid I cannot agree, because it would cost far more than the council has promised.

teaching.en: Although Tom voiced his dissent, the discussion was constructive: everybody wanted safer streets, and the only sticking point was the cost.
teaching.es: Aunque Tom expresó su desacuerdo, el debate fue constructivo: todos querían calles más seguras y el único obstáculo era el coste.
teaching.explanationEs: Voice dissent: expresar desacuerdo. Sticking point: el obstáculo concreto que bloquea un acuerdo.
segments: Although Tom voiced his dissent, the discussion was constructive: everybody wanted
safer streets, and the only sticking point was the cost.
teaching.audioText: Although Tom voiced his dissent, the discussion was constructive: everybody wanted safer streets, and the only sticking point was the cost.

teaching.en: I take your point, Leo, but the real obstacle is not the idea itself; it is finding a volunteer willing to manage the scheme.
teaching.es: Entiendo lo que dices, Leo, pero el verdadero obstáculo no es la idea, sino encontrar a un voluntario dispuesto a gestionar el proyecto.
teaching.explanationEs: I take your point reconoce lo dicho antes de discrepar; volunteer es quien se ofrece sin que se lo pidan.
segments: I take your point, Leo, but the real obstacle is not the

Then Mia offered to paraphrase the council's letter, so that everybody would be sure of the deadline, and Ana thanked her and asked the secretary to note it down.

To summarise: Leo wants a Saturday market, Mia would rather use Sundays for families, and Tom is concerned about the noise and the litter. 5. I would like to build on Leo's idea: we could run a trial for one month and then ask the neighbours what they think of it. 6. That is a different topic, so let us set it aside and stick to the agenda, please.

origin.text: Reunión de la asociación de vecinos sobre un mercado semanal. teaching.en: Good minutes are concise: they note each decision, say who will act and by when, and leave out the arguments that led to it.
teaching.es: Un acta bien hecha es concisa: anota cada decisión, dice quién actuará y para cuándo, y omite los argumentos que llevaron a ella.
teaching.explanationEs: El acta recoge tres datos: qué se decidió, quién lo hará y para cuándo; no transcribe el debate.

prompt.es: ¿Qué registra en el acta esta intervención de Ana?

choices.text: A decision taken by vote before the discussion began.
A member who warned he cannot come, and enough people to start.
An action given to Carlos with a date to finish it.

feedback.es: Ana anota la ausencia avisada de Carlos y confirma que hay quórum para empezar. Aún no hay votación ni acciones asignadas.

hint.es: Piensa en quién falta y en si quedan suficientes personas para decidir.

origin.text: Ana: Apologies were received from Carlos, who cannot attend tonight. As we still have a quorum, I suggest that we begin with the first item.

prompt.es: Completa: «Los miembros votaron aprobar el nuevo horario.»

feedback.es: Vote to approve + nombre es la fórmula del acta para una decisión tomada por votación; aquí diez votos superan a dos.

hint.es: Es el verbo que significa dar el visto bueno a algo tras votar.

origin.text: After a short debate, the chair asked for a show of hands. Ten members raised their hands in favour and two against, so the members voted to ___ the new timetable.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Como nadie tiene nada más que añadir, levanto la sesión.»

answer.text: As nobody has anything else to add I adjourn the meeting

feedback.es: Adjourn the meeting cierra la sesión cuando ya no quedan asuntos; as nobody has anything else explica el motivo.

hint.es: Empieza por la razón (As nobody…) y termina con el verbo que cierra la sesión.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué se acordó sobre la puerta del salón.

choices.text: Leo will repair the door before the next meeting.
The hall will close until the door has been fixed.
Tom will check the lock and tell the group by Wednesday.

feedback.es: Ana encarga a Tom revisar la cerradura y él promete informar el miércoles. Leo solo avisa del problema y el salón no se cierra.

origin.audio: It was nearly eight o'clock when Ana, who was chairing, looked around the hall and asked whether there was any other business. Leo mentioned that the door still did not close properly, and Sara reminded everyone that the same problem had been reported in March without any result. Ana asked Tom to check the lock, and he promised to report back by Wednesday. Nobody had anything else to add, so she thanked the members for coming and adjourned the meeting. The secretary said she would circulate the minutes within two days.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez. ¿Qué sugiere el comentario de Sara sobre marzo?

choices.text: That the problem has been ignored for too long.
That the problem only appeared this week.
That Leo reported the problem to the wrong person.

feedback.es: Sara recuerda que el problema ya se comunicó en marzo sin resultado: sugiere que se lleva meses sin atender, no que sea nuevo.

prompt.es: Redacta el acta con decisiones, responsables y plazos.

answer.text: Minutes of the neighbourhood club meeting, 12 May, 7 p.m. Chair: Ana. Secretary: Sara. Apologies were received from Carlos, who could not attend, but the meeting had a quorum, so the members were able to begin. Item 1: community garden. Leo proposed opening the garden on Saturdays and on Wednesday evenings. The chair asked for a vote, and the motion was carried, with Tom choosing to abstain. Action: Leo is responsible for speaking to the neighbours about the new opening times, and the deadline is 20 May. Item 2: summer party. Mia had reservations about the price, so the group agreed to look for a compromise. Action: Tom will ask the council for prices by Friday 15 May and report back at the next meeting. Any other business: none. The chair adjourned the meeting at 8 p.m., and the secretary will circulate these minutes within two days.

Minutes of the club meeting on 12 May at 7 p.m. The chair was Ana and the secretary was Sara. Apologies were received from Carlos, who cannot attend this month, and there was a quorum, so the meeting went ahead as planned. Item 1: the community garden. Leo proposed that it should open on Saturdays and on Wednesday evenings, and the members voted to approve this, although Tom abstained. Leo will speak to the neighbours about the new times by 20 May. Item 2: the summer party. Mia is not convinced that the price is fair, so the group will look for a compromise. Tom is responsible for asking the council for prices, and the deadline is Friday 15 May, when he will report back to the group. There was no other business, and the chair adjourned the meeting at 8 p.m.

feedback.es: Un acta completa recoge quién faltó, si había quórum, qué se votó, quién actúa y para cuándo, y cómo se cerró la sesión.

origin.text: Reunión del club de barrio, 12 de mayo, 19:00. Preside Ana y es secretaria Sara. Ausente con aviso: Carlos; hay quórum. Punto 1, huerto comunitario: Leo propone abrir los sábados y los miércoles por la tarde; se vota y se aprueba, con la abstención de Tom; Leo es responsable de hablar con los vecinos y el plazo es el 20 de mayo. Punto 2, fiesta de verano: Mia tiene dudas por el precio; se acuerda buscar un término medio; Tom pedirá precios al ayuntamiento antes del viernes 15 e informará en la próxima reunión. Otros asuntos: ninguno. Se levanta la sesión a las 20:00.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué se deduce de la abstención de Mia.

choices.text: That she voted against the new opening hours.
That she may change her view once she sees the numbers.
That she did not attend the meeting at all.

feedback.es: Mia no votó porque quiere ver las cifras antes; no vota en contra ni falta. La presidencia admite reabrir el asunto si los números cambian el panorama.

origin.audio: Let me make sure that we have this right before I close the item. The committee agreed to accept the new opening hours, although Mia did not vote because she wants to see the figures first. Tom will collect those figures and send them to everyone by the twentieth, and Sara will add them to the minutes. If the figures change the picture, we will reopen the matter at the June meeting.

prompt.es: Según el acta, ¿qué decisión se registra sobre la fiesta?

choices.text: The party was approved for 20 June in the park.
The proposal was rejected because of the cost.
The decision was put off until the council answers.

feedback.es: Los miembros acuerdan aplazar la decisión hasta que responda el ayuntamiento; la fecha del 20 de junio fue solo la propuesta de Sara.

origin.text: Item 3: the summer party. Sara proposed that the club hold the party in the park on 20 June. Tom had reservations about the cost, and Leo suggested asking the council for help. The members agreed to postpone the decision until the council replies. Action: Leo will write to the council by Friday.

prompt.es: Completa: «Decidió abstenerse en lugar de votar a favor o en contra.»

feedback.es: Abstain significa no votar ni a favor ni en contra; se registra en el acta como una abstención.

origin.text: Sara did not feel that she knew enough about the topic to take sides. She decided to ___ rather than vote for or against the motion.

prompt.es: ¿Qué da a entender la presidencia al aceptar aplazar el punto del huerto?

choices.text: That a vote with too few members present would not count.
That Leo had made a mistake when writing the agenda.
That the garden item had already been settled in May.

feedback.es: La presidencia acepta aplazar porque una decisión sin quórum no sería válida: con tantos miembros ausentes, la votación no contaría.

origin.text: The meeting was adjourned at 8.15 p.m. Before closing, Leo asked whether the garden item could be carried over to June, as several members had left early. The chair agreed, noting that a decision taken without a quorum would not be valid.

prompt.es: Escucha la confirmación y elige qué ocurrió con la moción.

choices.text: It failed, because one member did not vote.
It passed, although two members voted against it.
It was postponed until the first of September.

feedback.es: La moción salió adelante por ocho votos a dos; el miembro que no votó no cambia el resultado y el 1 de septiembre es la fecha de efecto.

origin.audio: For the record, let me confirm that a quorum was present and that the motion was carried by eight votes to two, with one member not voting. The decision takes effect on the first of September, and the treasurer will report back at the next meeting.

prompt.es: Redacta una línea del acta: decisión, responsable y plazo.

answer.text: The club voted unanimously to buy new balls. Sara is responsible for ordering them, and she will report back by 15 June.
accepted: The club voted unanimously to buy new balls. Sara is responsible for ordering them, and she will report back by 15 June.
The members decided unanimously to buy new balls. Sara will order them and report back by 15 June.

feedback.es: La línea une la decisión tomada, la persona responsable y la fecha límite, que es lo mínimo que debe recoger un acta.

origin.text: El club votó por unanimidad comprar balones nuevos. Sara es la responsable y informará al grupo antes del 15 de junio.
